description: Performance budgets on the production export: large tables, heavy dashboards and long processes (QRun-IO/qqq#710). Bundle budgets are checked separately by scripts/perf-budget.mjs.

rows.feature: large table: a 10,000-row, 40-column table opens with every column and the exact first page within budget
scenarios: all 40 columns have a sort header; the first 25 rows carry the exact computed values; the total reads 10,000
time from navigation to the first page is within PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.firstPageMs
negative: only one page of rows is in the DOM (25 rows, 1,000 cells), not the table

rows.feature: large table: 250-row pages of 40 columns render, page and reach the last page within budget
scenarios: page size 250 shows ids 10000..9751 with 10,000 cells within PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.pageMs
next page shows 9750..9501 and last page 250..1 (page 40), each within PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.pageMs; the backend is asked for skip/limit 250
negative: the DOM never holds more than one page (250 rows)

rows.feature: large table: sorting and filtering 10,000 rows return exact results within budget
scenarios: sorting by Name ascending shows Row 00001..Row 00025 within PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.queryMs
Count 04 equals 0 narrows to the 40 matching rows (the SQL answer) within PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.queryMs

rows.feature: heavy dashboard: 24 widgets (statistics, bar, line and pie charts, 100-row tables) load once each within budget
scenarios: every widget finishes loading within PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.dashboardMs of navigation
statistics show their exact counts, chart data tables their exact points, tables their 100 rows
negative: each widget's data is requested exactly once

rows.feature: long process: a 10-second job over 10,000 rows reports progress, polls at a bounded rate and shows its result promptly
scenarios: progress messages advance while the job runs; the result shows Row Count 10000 and the SQL total
the result appears within PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.processResultMs of the job finishing
negative: status is polled no more than once per POLL_INITIAL_MILLIS (1.5 s) and never concurrently
